_comment: RATIFIED Replacement-Cost Table v03 (RCT v03) — Gabriel, 2026-07-14, governor-level. Supersedes replacement-cost.v1.json, which was a FLAT firm-wide $125/$137.50/$150: no per-market variation at all, sitting at roughly HALF true all-in shallow-bay replacement cost. An understated replacement cost makes computed discounts too small, so deals fail the floor — the old table made ORA TOO STRICT and passed on deals that clear doctrine. The Basis floor and Basis score divide by this; rctVersion folds into inputsVersion, so bumping it correctly INVALIDATES every score cached under the old denominator (those scores are stale, not merely old). AUTHORITATIVE COPY: the acquisition-underwriting skill, 'Replacement Cost Table (RCT v03)'. If this file and that table disagree, THAT TABLE WINS and this file is the bug.
basis: RCT v03 — all-in replacement for Class B/C shallow-bay/flex (hard + soft + developer profit + financing; land EXCLUDED, added separately in the basis test). POINT = C&W 2025 hard cost (small tier) [SOURCED] x shallow-bay size premium ~+43% at 40K SF, from C&W's OWN size curve [SOURCED] x soft/profit/financing 1.30 [EST — the one unsourced input; LOW end chosen so the floor is HARDER than truth] x escalation 1.0487 [SOURCED — Turner BCI, lowest of three indices]. Band +/-10% => LOW = 0.90 x POINT. Coherence passes: every all-in exceeds hard cost at ~1.95x.
_fallback_note: `psf` is the CONSERVATIVE FALLBACK used ONLY when a deal's market is null or has no RCT row. It is the CHEAPEST market to build in (Chicago Cook County IL since v3.2; Kansas City MO before), which yields the STRICTEST floor. We never hand a deal a looser floor because we failed to identify its market.
_v3_2_note: rctVersion bumped v3.1 -> v3.2 on 2026-11-12 (Gabriel in-turn, PR-B of the 2026-11-12 doctrine-drift audit). Three content changes, all from acquisition-underwriting SKILL.md v4.45: (1) the Chicago Cook County IL row (SKILL.md 'Chicago-Greater Cook County IL', LOW 225.59 / POINT 250.66 / HIGH 275.73, C&W 2025 small tier 127.79, SOURCED; ratified by Gabriel in-turn 2026-11-12); (2) the fallback `psf` moves to that row, because it is now the cheapest market and the fallback rule is 'the cheapest market to build in' (the strictest floor) — before this an unknown-market deal priced on Kansas City's $227.90 LOW, looser than a ratified row; (3) the v4.37 Construction-Type Multiplier Schedule and the adder schedule, which the engine and drawer now apply (POINT x multiplier + adders, LOW/HIGH at +/-10%; every multiplier [EST], calibration-pending; unknown type = the PEMB value for the subject SF capped at 0.90). Every market row is the tilt-up baseline. The bump re-keys every cached acquisition score: those scores are stale.
_v3_1_note: rctVersion bumped v3 -> v3.1 on 2026-09-29 (OI-354, Gabriel in-turn). The table content changed (Louisville KY added, matching the skill's 2026-08-11 table) without a version change, and computeInputsVersion folds only the version STRING, so scores cached under the 9-market table (Louisville priced on the fallback) would never have been invalidated. The bump re-keys every cached acquisition score on purpose: those scores are stale, not merely old. Values of every pre-existing row are unchanged.
